h: Shabbat Sanctifies the Past and Future

p: בַּמְּכִילְתָּא (יִתְרוֹ) זָכוֹר וְשָׁמוֹר זָכוֹר מִלְּפָנָיו וְשָׁמוֹר מִלְּאַחֲרָיו וְכוּלֵּי
— The Mekhilta, Yitro, teaches: ‘Remember’ and ‘safeguard’—remember what precedes it and safeguard what follows it, etc.
הָעִנְיָן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א רמח סוֹף עַמּוּד א) יְבָרֶכְךָ הַשֵּׁם מִדְּכוּרָא וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ מִנּוּקְבָא יְבָרֶכְךָ הַשֵּׁם מִזָּכוֹר וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ מִשָּׁמוֹר.

— This is explained through the holy Zohar (I, 248a, end): ‘May Hashem bless you’ comes from the masculine aspect, ‘and safeguard you’ from the feminine; ‘May Hashem bless you’ comes from ‘remember,’ and ‘safeguard you’ from ‘safeguard.’

וְהַיְינוּ דְּבִרְכַּת הַשֵּׁם מוֹרָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַכְנִיס קְדוּשָּׁה וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה לַלֵּב וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר יְבָרֶכְךָ הַשֵּׁם בְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה אִיקְרֵי (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב ס א)

— The blessing of Hashem means that Hashem imparts holiness and words of Torah to the heart. Thus ‘May Hashem bless you’ uses the Name Havayah: ‘The Holy One, blessed be He, is called Torah’ (Zohar II, 60a).
וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ הַיְינוּ הַשְּׁמִירָה מִכָּל רָע וְזֶהוּ מִשָּׁמוֹר מִנּוּקְבָא בְּחִינַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִיא מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה
— ‘And safeguard you’ means protection from every evil. This derives from ‘safeguard,’ from the feminine aspect, the congregation of Israel, whose attribute is reverence.

וְעַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה נִשְׁמָר הָאָדָם מִלַּעֲבוֹר עַל מִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק הָרוֹאֶה הוּבָא תּוֹסְפוֹת סוֹטָה כב:) עֲשֵׂה מִיִּרְאָה שֶׁאִם בָּאתָ לִבְעוֹט דַּע שֶׁאַתָּה יָרֵא וְאֵין יָרֵא מְבַעֵט.

— Through reverence a person is safeguarded from violating prohibitions. As it is taught (Jerusalem Talmud, chapter HaRo'eh, cited by Tosafot, Sotah 22b): Act from fear, for if you come to rebel, know that you fear, and one who fears does not rebel.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 248a: “He opened: “May Hashem bless you from Zion, and see the good of Jerusalem.” “May Hashem bless you from Zion”: from there blessings emerge to water the garden. It comprises all blessings and gives them to her; afterward, “See the good of Jerusalem.” This shows that all blessings come from male and female. Similarly, “May Hashem bless you and guard you”: “May Hashem bless you”—from the male; “and guard you”—from the female. “May Hashem bless you”—from Remember; “and guard you”—from Guard. It is all one matter, for from both of them blessings emerge to the worlds. Therefore, “He blessed them, each according to his blessing.””

We learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called Torah; water means Torah, and Torah is none other than the Holy One, blessed be He.”

p: וְזֶהוּ זָכוֹר מִלְּפָנָיו שֶׁקְּדוּשַּׁת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת מוֹעִיל לְתַקֵּן יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָבְרוּ עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת זָכוֹר שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה דִּבְכְנִיסַת שַׁבָּת כְּתִיב וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד.

— This is ‘remember what precedes it’: Shabbat's holiness rectifies the preceding weekdays through the aspect of ‘remember,’ meaning Torah. At the entrance of Shabbat it is written, ‘God saw everything He had made, and behold, it was very good.’
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת רָאָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אַחַר קִלְקוּל שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁמִּזֶּה יִהְיֶה נַעֲשֶׂה טוֹב מְאֹד עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה
— Through the holiness of Shabbat, Hashem saw, after Adam's corruption, that this would become ‘very good’ through repentance out of love.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קפד א) דְּלֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא וְלֵית טָבָא אֶלָּא מִגּוֹ בִּישָׁא.
— This follows the teaching (Zohar II, 184a): There is no light except that which emerges from darkness, and no good except that which emerges from evil.
וְאִיתָא (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ בָּלָק) מֵאֲשֶׁר יָקַרְתָּ בְעֵינַי נִכְבַּדְתָּ יָקָר מִיבָּעֵי לֵיהּ וְכוּלֵּי מַאי יָקַרְתָּ מִכְּלָל דְּאִיהוּ מִגַּרְמֵיהּ אִתְיַקַּר וְכוּלֵּי

— It is taught (Zohar Chadash, Balak): ‘Because you became precious in My eyes, you were honored’—it should say ‘precious,’ etc. What is ‘you became precious’? It indicates that he made himself precious, etc.
וַאֲנִי אֲהַבְתִּיךָ דְּלֵית רְחִימוּ לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בַּהֲדֵי בַר נָשׁ בְּעָלְמָא אֶלָּא מַאן דְּתָב מֵחוֹבוֹי
— ‘And I have loved you’: the Holy One, blessed be He, has love for no person in the world except one who repents of his sins.

וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קכט סוֹף עַמּוּד א) זַכָּאִין אִינּוּן מָארֵיהוֹן דִּתְשׁוּבָה דְּהָא בְּשַׁעְתָּא חֲדָא בְּיוֹמָא חֲדָא בְּרֶגַע חֲדָא קְרִיבִין לְגַבֵּי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
— Likewise it is taught (Zohar I, 129a, end): Fortunate are the masters of repentance, for in one hour, in one day, in one moment, they draw close to the Holy One, blessed be He,
מַה דְּלָא הֲווֹ הָכִי אֲפִלּוּ לְצַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים דְּאִתְקְרִיבוּ גַּבֵּי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בְּכַמָּה שְׁנִין אַבְרָהָם וְכוּלֵּי
— in a way that even completely righteous people, who drew close to the Holy One, blessed be He, over many years, did not—Abraham, etc.

וְזֶהוּ זָכוֹר מִלְּפָנָיו שֶׁמּוֹעִיל לְתַקֵּן הֶעָבָר עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת בִּבְחִינַת תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ח) שֶׁיִּהְיֶה טוֹב מְאֹד וּזְדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת כִּזְכֻיּוֹת.

— This is ‘remember what precedes it’: Shabbat's holiness rectifies the past through repentance out of love, as explained in discourse 8, so that it becomes ‘very good’ and deliberate sins become merits.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 184a: “There is no light except that which emerges from darkness. When this side is subdued, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted on high and honored in His glory. There is no service of the Holy One except from within darkness, and no good except from within evil. When a person enters a bad path and abandons it, then the Holy One is exalted in His glory. Therefore the perfection of everything is good and evil together, followed by ascent in goodness. There is no good except that which emerges from evil; through this good His glory is exalted, and this is complete service.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, Balak 37–38: “Rabbi Elazar opened: “Because you have become precious in My eyes, you have been honored, and I have loved you; I will give people in your place, and nations in place of your life.” “You have become precious”: it should have said “precious”—“because you are precious in My eyes.” What is “you have become precious”? It implies that he made himself precious. This is certainly so: anyone who is guilty before the Holy One, blessed be He, is at first held in contempt and is an abomination before Him. After he reconsiders and repents of his sin, he has now made himself precious. The Holy One proclaims concerning him: “Because you have become precious”—you have made yourself precious. “In My eyes you have been honored, and I have loved you”: the Holy One has love for no person in the world except one who repents of his sin. Therefore, “I have loved you.””

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 129a: “Fortunate are the masters of repentance, for in one hour, in one day, in one moment they draw close to the Holy One, blessed be He, in a way that even the completely righteous did not attain except by drawing close to Him over many years. Avraham did not enter those supernal days until he was old, as explained. Likewise David, as it says, “King David was old, advanced in days.” But the master of repentance immediately enters and cleaves to the Holy One, blessed be He.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 21:3: “It is taught in the Mekhilta concerning ‘Remember’ and ‘Safeguard’: remember what precedes it and safeguard what follows it. That is, the holiness of the Shabbat day shines its holiness upon the six weekdays before it through the aspect of ‘remember,’ and the radiance of Shabbat's holiness also extends to the coming six weekdays through the aspect of ‘safeguard.’ … Besides this, on every Shabbat the power of repentance always shines, so that all past deeds are rectified through it, as on the first Shabbat of Creation, as it is said, ‘God saw everything He had made, and behold, it was very good’: that is, everything was rectified, even what seemed, Heaven forbid, to have been ruined, as the Sages expounded on ‘and behold, it was very good.’ Through this, ‘The heavens and the earth were completed,’ as vaychal is rendered ‘and He desired’: through the holiness of Shabbat all the deeds of the six weekdays that have passed become desirable. As the Midrash says, when Adam saw the power of repentance he began and said, ‘A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day: It is good to acknowledge,’ etc.”

It adds the reading of vaychal as ‘desire,’ by which the past week's deeds become desirable, and the Midrash of Adam's Shabbat psalm.

p: מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְאַחֲרָיו מוֹעִיל רַק בִּבְחִינַת שָׁמוֹר וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִשְׁמָר מִכָּל רָע בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאַחֲרָיו.
— For what follows, however, it works only through ‘safeguard,’ ‘and safeguard you’: protection from every evil during the following six weekdays.

וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּהַבְדָּלָה בַּתְּפִלָּה הָחֵל עָלֵינוּ הַיָּמִים הַבָּאִים וְכוּלֵּי חֲשׂוּכִים מִכָּל חֵטְא וְכוּלֵּי וּמְדוּבָּקִים בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיִּרְאָה לְהִשָּׁמֵר מִמִּצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ מֵהַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי.

— Thus in the Havdalah prayer we say, ‘Begin for us the coming days,’ etc., ‘withheld from every sin,’ etc., ‘and attached to fear of You.’ The root of reverence is safeguarding oneself against prohibitions, as we cited from the Jerusalem Talmud.
וּמִקּוֹדֶם אוֹמְרִים וַתְּלַמְּדֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת חוּקֵּי רְצוֹנֶךָ.
— Before this we say, ‘You taught us to perform the statutes of Your will.’

paragraphs.text: Saturday-night Amidah, “Attah chonantanu”: “You graciously granted us knowledge of Your Torah and taught us to perform the laws of Your will. You distinguished, Hashem our God, between holy and ordinary, between light and darkness, between Israel and the nations, between the seventh day and the six days of work. Our Father, our King, bring upon us the days approaching us in peace, withheld from every sin, cleansed of every iniquity, and attached to the fear of You.”

h: Bringing the Holiness of Shabbat into Work

p: וְהוּא דְּשַׁבָּת יוֹמָא דְנִשְׁמָתִין אִיהוּ וְלָאו יוֹמָא דְגוּפָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב רה סוֹף עַמּוּד א) וּנְשָׁמָה נִקְרָא שָׁמַיִם וְהַגּוּף אֶרֶץ
— Shabbat is the day of souls, not the day of the body, as stated in the Zohar (II, 205a, end). The soul is called heaven, and the body earth.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין צא:) הַשָּׁמַיִם מֵעָל זוֹ נְשָׁמָה וְאֶל הָאָרֶץ לָדִין עַמּוֹ זֶה הַגּוּף
— As it is taught (Sanhedrin 91b), ‘the heavens above’ refers to the soul, and ‘to the earth, to judge His people’ refers to the body.
וּבְשַׁבָּת הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל מֵאַנְשֵׁי שָׁמַיִם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם עֵסֶק בְּעִנְיְנֵי הַגּוּף וְהָאָרֶץ.
— On Shabbat a Jew is among the people of heaven, having no occupation with matters of the body and earth.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּיוֹם א׳ הַשִּׁיר שֶׁלּוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ.
— Therefore Sunday's psalm is ‘The earth and its fullness belong to Hashem.’
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יְשׁוּקְּעוּ כָּל כָּךְ בְּעִנְיְנֵי הָאָרֶץ וְהַגּוּף בִּימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּזְכְּרוּ שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— By remembering that everything comes from Hashem, they will not become so immersed in earthly and bodily matters during the weekdays.
וְהִנֵּה מִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִהְיוֹת מְשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת כְּהִלְכָתוֹ שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִהְיוֹת נִגְאָל מִכֹּל וָכֹל אָז זוֹכֶה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֶצְלוֹ יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה גַּם כֵּן כְּשַׁבָּת
— One who merits to observe Shabbat properly and thereby to be wholly redeemed merits to have his weekdays too become like Shabbat.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג כט ב) תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בְּנוֹי דְּמַלְכָּא וּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא אִתְקְרִיאוּ שַׁבָּתוֹת.
— As Ra'aya Meheimna teaches (Zohar III, 29b): Torah scholars, the children of the King and Queen, are called Shabbatot.

וּמוֹעִיל הַשַּׁבָּת לִהְיוֹת נֶחְקָק בַּלֵּב לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה תַּכְלִית מְכוּוָּן הַבְּרִיאָה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר לִהְיוֹת פָּנוּי רַק לְתוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה
— Shabbat engraves in the heart the resolve to act according to God's will, as was creation's intended purpose: ‘God made man upright,’ free solely for Torah and Divine service.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוֹף קִידּוּשִׁין) וַאֲנִי נִבְרֵאתִי לְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת קוֹנִי.
— As stated at the end of Kiddushin, ‘I was created to serve my Maker.’
רַק אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל שֶׁנִּתְקַלֵּל בְּזֵיעַת אַפֶּיךָ תֹּאכַל לֶחֶם אָז מִצְוָתוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם לִשְׁבּוֹת רַק בְּשַׁבָּת וּבִימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הוּתְּרָה הַמְּלָאכָה.
— Only after the corruption, when man was cursed with ‘By the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread,’ did God's command become to rest only on Shabbat, while labor was permitted during the weekdays.
אֲבָל רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם הוּא שֶׁיְּהֵא הָאָדָם דְּרוּפְתְּקֵי דְאוֹרַיְיתָא
— But God's will is that a person should be a bearer of the toil of Torah.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּפֵרוּשׁ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת לה:) וּבִזְמַן שֶׁאֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם מְלַאכְתָּן נַעֲשֵׂית עַל יְדֵי עַצְמָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר
— As we explained the teaching (Berakhot 35b), when Israel do not fulfill God's will, they perform their work themselves: ‘You shall gather your grain,’ etc.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעוֹשִׂין כְּמִצְוָתוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְשׁוֹבְתִין בְּשַׁבָּת (וְנִתְבָּאֵר פָּרָשַׁת לֶךְ מַאֲמָר ג)
— They do fulfill God's command, working during the six weekdays and resting on Shabbat, as explained in Lech Lecha, discourse 3.
אַךְ עַל כָּל פָּנִים כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל זוֹכֶה עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת לִימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאַחֲרָיו.
— Nevertheless, every Jew gains through Shabbat's holiness a benefit for the weekdays that follow.
שֶׁאַף אִם הוּא מוּכְרָח לַעֲסוֹק בִּמְלָאכָה לְצוֹרֶךְ פַּרְנָסָתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה לִהְיוֹת דְּרוּפְתְּקֵי דְאוֹרַיְיתָא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְלַאכְתּוֹ נַעֲשֵׂית עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים.
— Even if he must work for his livelihood, not having merited to be wholly devoted to Torah with his work performed by others,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל כָּל פָּנִים לֹא יְשׁוּקַּע כָּל כָּךְ בָּזֶה וְיִזְכּוֹר כִּי לַהַשֵּׁם הָאָרֶץ
— he will at least not become so immersed in it and will remember that the earth belongs to Hashem.
וְאַף בְּעִנְיְנֵי הַגּוּף שֶׁמְּכוּנֶּה בְּשֵׁם אֶרֶץ נִמְצָא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
— Even within bodily matters, designated as earth, the will of Hashem is present.
וְהוּא הַמְכַוֵּון לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְקַדֵּשׁ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה רְשׁוּת לִהְיוֹת כְּמִצְוָה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ כַּמָּה פְעָמִים וְזֶהוּ שָׁמוֹר לְאַחֲרָיו:

— This is one who directs his intention for the sake of Heaven, thereby sanctifying an optional action so that it becomes like a mitzvah, as we have said many times. This is ‘safeguard what follows it.’

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 82b: “Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: In all my days I have not seen a deer gathering figs, a lion carrying burdens, or a fox keeping a shop, yet they earn their livelihood without suffering. They were created only to serve me, while I was created to serve my Maker. If those who were created only to serve me earn their livelihood without suffering, should I, who was created to serve my Maker, not earn my livelihood without suffering? paragraphs.text: Berakhot 35b: “Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: Can a person plow at plowing time, sow at sowing time, reap at reaping time, thresh at threshing time, and winnow when the wind blows—what will become of Torah? paragraphs.text: Parallel: Yisrael Kedoshim §8 (Har Bracha edition, p. 114): “Our Sages said in Megillah (16b): “Light”—this is Torah, the holiness of Israel that comes from its root. “Joy”—this is a festival, the holiness that comes from sacred times. Although their foundation is Shabbat, whose holiness is fixed and established, the essential establishment of its holiness in the hearts of the children of Israel occurs when it brings holiness into the weekdays as well. From this comes the holiness of the six festival days, which Israel sanctifies: their sanctification draws onward the holiness Israel has brought about during the weekdays.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: The effect upon the weekdays is central to what it means for Shabbat’s holiness to become settled in the heart. Rav Tzadok also gives those weekdays a productive role: holiness brought into them contributes to Israel’s sanctification of the festivals. This develops the present maamar’s claim that Shabbat changes the character of weekday work, including the intention that makes an optional action holy.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Yitro 13:3: “Shabbat is the day of souls and not the day of the body, as stated in the holy Zohar (Vayakhel 205a, end), and then Israel are called children of heaven, in the sense of (Sanhedrin 91b) ‘He calls to the heavens above’: this is the soul; and the superiority of Israel is recognizable. During the weekdays, when a Jew too enters earthly matters, the needs of the body, the distinction between Israel and the nations is not so recognizable. But they said (Mekhilta on this portion): ‘Remember’ and ‘safeguard’: remember what precedes it and safeguard what follows it. That is, from the holiness of Shabbat there remains for Israel the anticipation and hope in the heart for the holiness of the coming Shabbat, in the manner of Rashi's explanation of ‘and his father safeguarded the matter’: he was waiting and anticipating when it would come. This is ‘safeguard what follows it’: he waits and anticipates the Shabbat day, when he will be free only for Torah and the service of Hashem, as man was created to serve his Maker and to be among the people of heaven, and his occupation with bodily needs is only out of necessity after the curse. Through this the distinction between Israel and the nations is recognized even during the weekdays, and for this Havdalah is made over the cup: we rejoice in perceiving the distinction.”
